title: How do snakes slither without legs?
examples: How can a snake move with no legs?
Why can't snakes slither on glass?

explain.say: A snake has no legs, but it has hundreds of vertebrae and ribs worked by strong muscles. In its commonest way of moving, waves of muscle contraction bend the body into S-shaped curves.

explain.say: Each curve presses sideways against rocks, twigs and bumps. The ground pushes back; the side-to-side parts of those pushes cancel out, leaving a push forward, so the body follows the head along one wavy path.

explain.say: Wide belly scales help too. They catch on rough ground like the bristles of a brush, resisting sliding backwards or sideways while gliding easily forwards.

explain.say: Where there is nothing to push against, snakes switch styles. In tunnels they move like a concertina, desert sidewinders throw loops sideways, and heavy pythons creep in a straight line on their belly scales.

faq.q: How can a snake move with no legs?
faq.a: A snake bends its long body into curves using muscles attached to its many ribs and vertebrae. The curves push against the ground and things around it, and the ground pushes back, sliding the snake forward.

faq.q: Why can't snakes slither on glass?
faq.a: On smooth glass there are no bumps to push against and the belly scales cannot grip, so the curves just slide sideways. A snake on a very smooth surface wriggles a lot but goes almost nowhere.
asks: Can snakes move on smooth floors?

faq.a: Sidewinding is used by some desert snakes on loose sand. The snake lifts parts of its body and throws them sideways, touching the sand at only a couple of points, so it moves diagonally and leaves J-shaped tracks.

faq.q: How does a python move in a straight line?
faq.a: Big, heavy snakes can use rectilinear motion. Muscles lift sections of belly skin forward, plant them so the scales grip, then pull the body along over them, like a caterpillar, in a straight line.

faq.q: How many bones does a snake have?
faq.a: A snake can have a few hundred vertebrae, often between about 200 and 400, and most carry a pair of ribs. That is what makes the body so flexible.
asks: How many ribs does a snake have?

facts: Snakes have from about 200 to more than 400 vertebrae, most bearing a pair of ribs.
A sidewinding snake touches the hot sand at only a few points at a time.

quiz.say: Why does a snake struggle to move across a smooth glass sheet?
quiz.show: Why does a snake struggle to move across a smooth glass sheet?

options.show: Nothing to push on and scales can't grip
options.say: Nothing to push on and scales can't grip

quiz.why: Slithering needs bumps to push against and friction for the belly scales; glass offers neither.

wrong.1: Temperature is not the main problem; even warm glass is too smooth.
wrong.2: Snakes never use legs; they need grip and bumps.

quiz.say: A snake is moving through a narrow tunnel. Which style is it most likely using?
quiz.show: A snake is moving through a narrow tunnel. Which style is it most likely using?
quiz.why: In a tunnel the snake anchors part of its body against the walls and stretches the rest forward, like a concertina.

wrong.1: Sidewinding is for loose sand in the open, not tight tunnels.
wrong.2: Snakes do not leap to travel through tunnels.
